text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and latency observed for Hosted API in eu-west-2 and several Dedicated pools. Alert group: api.euw2.5xx_high (threshold 2%), current 7.8% over 5m.

anne (SRE): grabbing this. can someone post initial impact assessment? are customers impacted or just internal health metrics?

mike (infra): seeing backend STS errors from eu-west-2 on control-plane auth calls. lots of 503s to sts.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com. also Datadog ingest for eu-west-2 shows backlog / delayed metrics.

olivia (dedicated-oncall): confirmed Dedicated pool euw2-dedicated-1 showing increased request latency and ~3% 5xx on inference endpoints. routing to backup regions not fully active; some traffic still pinned.

sam (prod-ops): customers on EU clusters may see increased latency or failed requests. no widespread data loss reported. creating post to status page draft.

anne (SRE): timeline: 1732004567 alert triggered. preliminary root: external auth (AWS STS) returning 5xx which causes control-plane token fetches to fail -> worker auth fallbacks and higher latencies. Datadog ingest lag means observability alerts delayed which slowed detection.

mike (infra): reproducing STS call:
```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null https://sts.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com | head -n 5
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: text/xml
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2023 12:02:40 GMT
Retry-After: 30
```

mike (infra): logs from control-plane auth proxy: `auth-proxy[euw2] ERROR fetch_token: upstream error 503 (AWS STS)` repeated.

anne (SRE): immediate mitigations: 1) enable routing fallback to nearest healthy region for new inbound traffic (force route eu-west-1/us-west-2) 2) temporarily increase control-plane auth cache TTL to avoid token fetch on every request 3) scale Dedicated pool capacity for eu-west-2 to absorb retry storms 4) notify customers on status.redwood.ai (drafted).

olivia (dedicated-oncall): doing TTL bump now. patch:
```yaml
auth_cache_ttl_seconds: 600  # was 60
```

deploy-bot: Starting rollout of config auth_cache_ttl_seconds=600 to control-plane (canary -> euw2 -> global).

deploy-bot: Canary succeeded (euw2-canary), rolling to euw2 (3/3 hosts).

mike (infra): routing change ready. policy snippet:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  - match: region=="eu-west-2"
    fallback_regions: ["eu-west-1","us-west-2"]
    allow_partial: true
    prefer_local: false
```
apply: `redwoodctl routes apply --policy-file /tmp/euw2-fallback.yml`

mike (infra): applied. routing metrics show ~42% of new sessions now routed out of eu-west-2.

anne (SRE): scaling Dedicated pools + orchestration: `k8s scale deployment/euw2-dedicated-1 --replicas=12` to handle retries.

olivia (dedicated-oncall): scaled. observed queued requests draining. 5xx trending down but latency still elevated ~200ms above normal.

sam (prod-ops): status page posted: "Customers in eu-west-2 may experience increased latency and intermittent 5xx due to upstream AWS STS degradation. We are routing traffic to backup regions and applying mitigations. Next update in 30 minutes." link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20230921-euw2

anne (SRE): contacting AWS support & checking AWS Health Dashboard. AWS Health: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ indicates "europe (eu-west-2) STS: Investigating". also opened support case #1234567890.

mike (infra): reaching out to Datadog support; found active incident: https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/abcd1234 "Metric intake delay in eu-west-2" — that's why our dashboards didn't alert earlier.

olivia (dedicated-oncall): customer impact update: a handful of high-traffic tenants on Dedicated have seen retries and transient failures. no data corruption. we've enabled per-tenant ephemeral routing overrides for top 10 tenants to route them to eu-west-1 immediately.

sam (prod-ops): emailing affected customers with mitigation steps + ETA. template: "We're experiencing elevated errors in eu-west-2 due to upstream AWS auth. We have routed your traffic to eu-west-1; no action required. We'll follow up when STS is back to normal."

anne (SRE): ongoing tasks assigned:
- anne (lead incident) -> coordinate AWS & Datadog comms, own postmortem
- mike -> monitor routing effectiveness & ensure no token leakage across regions
- olivia -> watch Dedicated pool health and customer overrides
- sam -> customer comms & status page updates

mike (infra): note: watch out for region-hopping latency penalties; for latency-sensitive customers we can keep sticky sessions. added a sticky override option in routing config.

olivia (dedicated-oncall): implemented sticky override for top tenants. verifying telemetry for session affinity.

deploy-bot: Auth cache TTL rollout completed across control-plane.

anne (SRE): update 1732004600: 5xx rate dropped from 7.8% -> 2.1% after routing + cache TTL. still above baseline but improving. Datadog ingest backlog cleared slowly; some dashboards now accurate.

mike (infra): AWS STS still showing intermittent 503s in eu-west-2 but traffic routed away. support case updated with our mitigation steps.

sam (prod-ops): next customer update posted. scheduled another update in 30m or on next status change.

anne (SRE): handoff plan: olivia will be primary for next 2 hours monitoring Dedicated; i'll stay as incident lead until STS cleared and 24h stable. if STS persists >2h escalate to oncall manager.

olivia (dedicated-oncall): ack, taking watch.

mike (infra): leaving a quick runbook note for postmortem: root likely AWS STS regional degradation + observability ingestion lag. mitigation steps that worked: routing fallback, auth cache TTL increase, scale dedicated pools, per-tenant overrides. will add perf/cost impact numbers to postmortem.

anne (SRE): closing interim: incident de-escalation -> monitoring. creating incident ticket INC-20230921-EUW2 for postmortem and RCA.

sam (prod-ops): thanks everyone. short retrospective scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20230921-EUW2 created and assigned to anne (SRE).
